title: Google Cloud MCP Server
summary: Let the agent run gcloud commands through Google's MCP server (npx), under your own account or a limited service account.
description: Google's gcloud MCP server exposes a single tool that runs gcloud commands. It lets an agent list projects, inspect resources and run the same operations you would type in a terminal, minus a deny list of interactive or arbitrary-input commands.
It has no credentials of its own: it uses the account active in your gcloud CLI. To narrow what it can do, authorize gcloud as a service account with a restricted role and use impersonation.
useWhen: List Compute Engine instances across a project
Check which APIs are enabled before deploying
Look at Cloud Run service revisions
Inspect IAM bindings on a project

mcp.name: gcloud
access: Runs gcloud commands with the active gcloud account permissions
Can change cloud resources if that account is allowed to

example.prompt: List my Cloud Run services in europe-west1 and show which have more than one revision serving traffic.
example.result: 4 services. checkout-api splits traffic 90/10 across two revisions; the other 3 serve a single revision.

faq.question: What do I need installed?
faq.answer: Node.js 20 or newer and the gcloud CLI, already signed in.

faq.question: How do I keep it safe?
faq.answer: Authorize gcloud as a service account that has a narrow role, since the server's rights equal those of the active account.

access: Runs gcloud commands on your machine
Permissions equal the active gcloud account
